title: GUI pattern splitting breaks advertised brace alternatives
steps: Compare patterns/left and patterns/right; enter *.{java,kt} in the filename filter.
Under Options, try the exclude pattern *.{txt,rs}. Compare with the working include list *.java *.kt.
actual: Both brace expressions fail with unclosed alternate group. The include is split into *.{java and kt}; the exclude is similarly split at its comma. Passing ["*.{java,kt}"] directly to the production run_compare command succeeds and finds 3 files.
cause: applyPatterns splits on every space, comma and semicolon; applyExcludes splits every comma. Neither tokenizer respects brace groups or character classes.
fix: Use a shared glob-aware list tokenizer that preserves separators inside groups/classes, and define quoting/escaping for literal separators. Regressions: brace alternatives, nested groups/classes, normal multi-pattern lists, invalid syntax recovery, Enter/debounce/Escape.
notes: Related UX limitation: literal filenames containing spaces, commas or semicolons cannot be entered exactly; quotes/backslash-space do not provide a working escape. Direct backend patterns for those exact filenames work. The help explicitly advertises brace alternatives.

title: Question-mark matching and case folding are byte/ASCII based for Unicode names
steps: Include files a.txt, é.txt, 中.txt, 😀.txt and Ä.TXT. Apply ?.txt, ??.txt, ???.txt and ????.txt.
Try ä.txt against Ä.TXT; compare with the working exact pattern Ä.txt.
actual: The single ? excludes é/中/😀/Ä. Two ? match é/Ä, three match 中, and four match 😀, following UTF-8 byte lengths. ä.txt finds nothing while Ä.txt finds the file. ASCII extension case folding works.
cause: Includes uses globset byte-oriented matching and ASCII case folding. The tooltip promises one character and case does not matter without explaining this restriction.
fix: Choose Unicode scalar/case-fold semantics for displayed UTF-8 filenames, with an explicit policy for undecodable paths, or accurately restrict/document the contract. Regressions must cover accented letters, CJK, emoji, mixed extension case and Unicode case pairs.

title: Filtered archive copy overwrites hidden entries behind a one-file confirmation
steps: Compare archive-warning/left and archive-warning/right; set *.txt. Both bundle.zip files contain keep.txt and a different hidden.bin.
Select the bundle.zip container and choose Copy right. The native confirmation says Copying replaces 1 file and lists bundle.zip/keep.txt.
Confirm and inspect the right ZIP with Python zipfile.
actual: The right hidden.bin is replaced by the left hidden.bin, although it was hidden and absent from the one-file replacement confirmation. A control copying an ordinary filtered directory preserves its hidden .bin.
cause: The comparison opens archives to find matching children, and the confirmation counts only filtered descendants. ops::copy takes the local archive fast path and copies the entire container as a raw file.
fix: Use one operation plan for preview/confirmation/execution. Either merge only the selected matching entries while preserving unrelated destination entries, or explicitly present and confirm whole-archive replacement including hidden content. Do not promise one child replacement and execute a raw container overwrite. Test include and exclude filters, ZIP/nested archives and normal-folder controls.
notes: Related to #9/R03, but the normal filtered-directory copy passes here. This is the archive-container path on latest main; it is distinct from #12/H04 stale archive caching.

title: Copying a filtered parent skips visible matching files inside nested archives
steps: Compare nested-copy/left and nested-copy/right and enter *.txt. Expand wrapper/bundle.zip; keep.txt and wrapper/normal.txt are visible differences.
Select wrapper and Copy right; confirm the replacement and inspect the result.
actual: normal.txt is copied, but bundle.zip/keep.txt retains the right-hand content and remains Different. The selected visible archive descendant was silently skipped.
cause: Filter::keeps admits ordinary directories but an Archive entry only if the archive name/path itself matches. The comparison walks archive containers even when only their children match, so recursive copy traverses a different set of entries.
fix: Share the comparison and copy traversal/selection semantics, including filtered archive descendants. Resolve this alongside W03: simply admitting whole archives would overwrite hidden entries. Verify all visible selected descendants are copied and unrelated hidden entries survive.

title: No-match filters leave identical Git folders visible in hierarchy view
steps: Compare git@base and git@same from the portable fixture. Both have an identical sub/inner.txt subtree.
Enter missing*.txt, then Expand and switch to Flat.
actual: Hierarchy view keeps sub as an empty Same folder while All files is 0. Expanding leaves it visible; Flat correctly shows no rows. The filter help says folders without matching files are left out.
cause: The Git quick-ID shortcut returns an unexpanded node before testing the include filter. Empty-container pruning deliberately keeps unexpanded nodes, and expanding later does not prune the parent row.
fix: Make lazy identical-subtree handling filter-aware and prune known-empty containers after expansion/refresh, while preserving the Git tree-ID performance benefit. Test no-match and selective matching filters in hierarchy, Expand and Flat.

title: Filesystem refresh inserts nonmatching files into an active wildcard filter
steps: Compare live/left and live/right with keep.txt and existing.bin; apply *.txt so only keep.txt is visible.
Externally modify left/existing.bin and create left/new.bin. Wait for the watcher.
Click Refresh without changing the pattern.
actual: The unchanged *.txt view grows from 1 to 3 files, showing both .bin files. Full Refresh restores the correct single .txt row. Both existing hidden and newly created nonmatching files leak into the view.
cause: refreshTarget picks the changed path, refresh_paths calls compare_path on it as a root, and root-file comparison does not apply the include predicate. replaceNode inserts the returned node without checking the current filter.
fix: Apply the same includes/excludes and ancestor coverage rules to incremental refresh as to full traversal, returning null for a nonmatching leaf and pruning empty parents. Test existing/new hidden files, matching files, nested paths, ancestor-matching globs, flat/status filters and pattern changes during pending refresh.
